title: A sheaf of sets is covered by extensions of finite constant sheaves on basis opens
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal B$ a basis of its topology, and $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Then there are a set $I$, opens $U_i\in\mathcal B$, finite sets $S_i$ ($i\in I$), and a morphism $\coprod_{i\in I}j_{U_i!}\underline{S_i}\to\mathcal F$ which is an epimorphism in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$, where $j_{U_i!}\underline{S_i}$ is the extension by the empty set of the sheaf of locally constant $S_i$-valued maps on $U_i$ [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty] and $\coprod$ is a coproduct in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. (One may take every $S_i$ to be a one-point set.)

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 0CAH (lemma-surjection), line 2992 and proof: choose basis neighbourhoods of germs and use the adjunction for j_! (00A3)

proof.text: *Step 1 (a basis section for every germ).* For $x\in X$ let $\mathcal F_x=\varinjlim_{W\ni x}\mathcal F(W)$ be the stalk, the colimit of sets over the open neighbourhoods of $x$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with germs $t\mapsto t_x$. Let $I$ be the set of pairs $i=(x,\sigma)$ with $x\in X$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal F_x$. For each $i=(x,\sigma)$ choose an open $W\ni x$ and $t\in\mathcal F(W)$ with $t_x=\sigma$ (every element of a colimit of sets is the image of an element of some term), then $U_i\in\mathcal B$ with $x\in U_i\subseteq W$ ($\mathcal B$ is a basis), and put $s_i=t|_{U_i}\in\mathcal F(U_i)$; then $(s_i)_x=t_x=\sigma$, since the germ of a restriction is the germ. Let $S=\{*\}$ be a one-point set and $S_i=S$ for all $i$; it is finite.

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 0CAH (label lemma-surjection, line 2992), proof, first two sentences

proof.text: *Step 2 (a section is a map from $j_{U!}\underline S$).* Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. The sheaf $\underline S_U$ of [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty] has $\underline S_U(V)=\{c_V\}$, the single (constant) map $V\to\{*\}$, for every open $V\subseteq U$, restrictions sending $c_V$ to $c_{V'}$. Setting $\alpha_V(c_V)=s|_V$ defines a morphism $\alpha:\underline S_U\to\mathcal F|_U$ of sheaves on $U$ (naturality is $(s|_V)|_{V'}=s|_{V'}$). By part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty-adjunction] there is a unique morphism $\psi:j_{U!}\underline S\to\mathcal F$ with $\psi\circ\theta=\tilde\alpha$, where $\theta:j_{U,p!}\underline S_U\to j_{U!}\underline S$ is the sheafification map and $\tilde\alpha_V=\alpha_V$ for $V\subseteq U$. Put $e_U=\theta_U(c_U)\in(j_{U!}\underline S)(U)$ (note $(j_{U,p!}\underline S_U)(U)=\underline S_U(U)$ as $U\subseteq U$). Then $\psi_U(e_U)=\tilde\alpha_U(c_U)=\alpha_U(c_U)=s$. Apply this to each $i\in I$: we get $\psi_i:j_{U_i!}\underline S\to\mathcal F$ and $e_i\in(j_{U_i!}\underline S)(U_i)$ with $\psi_{i,U_i}(e_i)=s_i$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 0CAH (label lemma-surjection, line 2992), proof, third sentence, citing Sheaves, Lemma Tag 00A3 (sheaves.tex label lemma-j-shriek, line 4549), part (2)

proof.text: *Step 3 (the coproduct and the total map).* The family $(j_{U_i!}\underline S)_{i\in I}$ is a diagram of sheaves of sets indexed by the discrete category $I$; by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-colimit-sheafification] it has a colimit in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$, i.e. a coproduct $\mathcal C=\coprod_{i\in I}j_{U_i!}\underline S$ with coprojections $\iota_i:j_{U_i!}\underline S\to\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] (concretely the sheafification of $V\mapsto\coprod_i(j_{U_i!}\underline S)(V)$). By its universal property there is a unique morphism $\Phi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal F$ with $\Phi\circ\iota_i=\psi_i$ for all $i\in I$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 0CAH (label lemma-surjection, line 2992), proof, display: the map from the coproduct over all (x, s)

proof.text: *Step 4 ($\Phi$ is surjective on stalks).* Let $x\in X$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal F_x$, and let $i=(x,\sigma)\in I$; then $x\in U_i$. The section $c=\iota_{i,U_i}(e_i)\in\mathcal C(U_i)$ satisfies $\Phi_{U_i}(c)=(\Phi\circ\iota_i)_{U_i}(e_i)=\psi_{i,U_i}(e_i)=s_i$ by Steps 2 and 3, so the stalk map $\Phi_x:\mathcal C_x\to\mathcal F_x$, $\Phi_x(c'_x)=(\Phi_V(c'))_x$, sends $c_x$ to $(s_i)_x=\sigma$ (Step 1). Hence $\Phi_x$ is surjective for every $x\in X$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 0CAH (label lemma-surjection, line 2992), proof, last sentence: 'is surjective on stalks'

proof.text: *Step 5 (epimorphism).* By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-epi-iff-stalks], a morphism of sheaves of sets on $X$ that is surjective on all stalks is an epimorphism in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$; so $\Phi:\coprod_{i\in I}j_{U_i!}\underline{S_i}\to\mathcal F$ (with $U_i\in\mathcal B$ and $S_i=\{*\}$ finite) is the required epimorphism.
